application.name: Stitching
application.description: Four synthetic fisheye cameras on a rig driving through a checkered world, stitched by holoscan-stitching's StitchOp into a bird's-eye surround view and a 360-degree panorama, shown by HoloViz in a window or rendered offscreen, with every output checked against the ground truth rendered directly from the world.

changelog.1.0.0: Initial release: the holoscan-stitching demo, with a synthetic surround rig, a bird's-eye view and a panorama, a HoloViz window or offscreen render, and checks against the ground truth.

hardware.name: NVIDIA GPU
hardware.description: A CUDA-capable GPU supported by the Holoscan SDK.

hardware.name: Display
hardware.description: For the window mode only; the offscreen and ci modes need none.

window.description: Live: four 1280x720 fisheye cameras at 30 frames per second, a 1024x1024 bird's-eye view and a 4096x1024 cylindrical panorama, shown in a HoloViz window until it is closed.

offscreen.description: HoloViz renders offscreen into CUDA memory: 60 frames, each output checked against the ground truth and each render checked.

ci.description: Finite headless check: 30 frames of the moving rig with different camera exposures and exposure compensation, a 1024x1024 bird's-eye view and a 4096x1024 panorama, each checked against the ground truth: PSNR, coverage, brightness and every checkerboard corner within 1 pixel.
